title: Permissions: the reading decision order
sourceBehaviour: Lcn ranks one reading: deny 6; a soft ask 3, else a matched-rule or bypass-immune safety-check ask 5, else ask 4; passthrough 2; allow 1, or 0 when the reason is entirely a rule (ize).
jwe treats an ask as soft when it has no matched ask rule and its reason is absent, type 'other', or all-soft subcommand results.
m0 is utt(decisionReason) or matchedAskRule.ruleBehavior === 'ask'; utt finds a rule ask anywhere in the reason tree.

Dl walks the reason tree for a safetyCheck the predicate accepts; X3 accepts a circuit breaker named in trn with bypassImmune true (dangerousRemoval, isolatePeerMachines, restrictedMode, outsideReadsBlocked).

DTr: a deny anywhere wins; a primary ask that is not soft returns before any ranking; otherwise the highest Lcn wins; a non-exhaustive set whose winner is not an ask becomes the synthetic 'Variables set in front of a declaration...' ask.
ior projects the combined result through sfn, then downgrades a soft ask from the alternates to a passthrough carrying its message and reason unless the primary is already a passthrough.
$pn reroutes an auto-mode allow to an ask with decisionReason {type: 'other', reason: srn}; jwe treats that reason as soft. The reroute is gated by hor and runs after the permission check.

The entry $pn ends by converting every surviving passthrough to an ask: let $e=V.behavior==='passthrough'?{...V,behavior:'ask',message:Rl(e.name,V.decisionReason)}:V, then return $e ([3364091,3364185), body16 5beadd59c5d65458; tail through return $e at [3364091,3364304)).
sfn turns an other-reason ask with a known bashMissKind into the read-block ask when blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories is on.
$cn upgrades an ask with a prefix ask rule to matchedAskRule.
hostAdaptations: applyShellReadings collects alternates with the deny scan first, ranks the primary with the alternates, lets the highest rank win, and keeps the synthetic non-exhaustive ask with the host's existing wording.

readingRank maps the host's decision space: deny 6; floor 'rule' ask 5 (the matchedAskRule equivalent); any other ask 4; allow 1. The source's soft ask 3, passthrough 2 and rule-only allow 0 have no host producer: an allow carries no reason tree, no reading result is a passthrough, and every host ask carries a mode or rule reason.

The host applies its mode hold inside decideOnce, so a mode ask reaches the ranking with no floor and ranks 4. The recovered order applies the hold after the reading combination; for every host-producible case, ranking the hold as a plain ask gives the same decision, because a rule ask from an alternate still outranks it and it still outranks an allow.
ior's soft-ask downgrade is not ported: the host produces no soft ask, and the entry $pn turns every passthrough back into an ask, so the downgrade could not end in an allow.
The alternate-ask winner keeps its own floor and is reported with the reading that raised it.
The bypass guard on the synthetic ask is the host's standing stand-in for the source mode short-circuit and is unchanged.
Not ported: sfn's read-block projection, $cn's matched-ask upgrade (decideOnce already returns floor 'rule' per reading), and the X3 bypass-immune checks (no host safety-check reasons).

knownLimitations: The host applies its mode hold inside decideOnce, before the reading combination, so the hold ranks as a plain ask instead of being applied after the combination as the recovered order does. For every host-producible case the decision is the same.
The host has no producer for a soft ask, a passthrough or a rule-only allow, so those Lcn ranks have no host input and ior's soft-ask downgrade is not ported.
sfn's read-block projection is not ported: the host has no read-block ask.
The X3 bypass-immune safety checks have no host producer.

findings: High: the ior downgrade was ported as 'return the primary allow', so in auto mode an alternate soft ask let the command run. The entry $pn converts every passthrough back to an ask, so the recovered result is never an allow. Repaired by removing the soft-ask rank and the downgrade; the alternate ask now always wins as an ask.

Medium: the record and the source comment claimed passthrough 'maps to allow' and that the auto hold is the $pn reroute. The reroute is gated by hor and runs after ior, so it cannot be a DTr input. Repaired by stating the host adaptation: the mode hold ranks as a plain ask and no soft ask exists to downgrade.
Low: the autoRuleAsk assertion also passes on the previous build. Kept as a guard; the distinguishing compiled baseline is the auto case, which the previous build allows.
Low: --baseline was not pinned to a build. The baseline branch now asserts the 4a1b14b build's answers, and the baseline identity is recorded.
